traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 211 Burseraceae: trees or shrubs giving resin or oil (frankincense, myrrh); leaves alternate, rarely opposite, compound, rarely of one leaflet; no stipules; flowers small, bisexual or of one sex; sepals and petals 3 to 5; stamens as many or twice as many as the petals; ovary superior, of 2 to 5 cells; fruit a drupe, or opening late. The flowers' regularity is from common knowledge (Hutchinson does not say), inferred.

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia, Burseraceae (read 2026-10-16): plants tend to be dioecious with unisexual flowers.
